figures.caption: Fig. 2. Development of the ionic concentration proﬁle in the electrolyte, calculated according to Eq. (14), during constant-current charging (1.0 C-rate) and relaxation upon current interruption after 50 min.

Fig. 3. Development of the electric ﬁeld in the electrolyte, calculated according to Eq. (19), under the same conditions of Fig. 2. is close to zero, and reaches a value of about −1200 V/m. This high electric ﬁeld region is, however, quite narrow and its overall con- tribution to the total overpotential are therefore rather moderate. Contrastingly, the electric ﬁeld is low near the positive electrode, where c(L,t) is large. This behaviour is explained by the presence of c(y,t) in denominator of the Eq. (19). Obviously, in order to build up non-uniform electric ﬁeld in the electrolyte as shown in Fig. 3, ionic charge separation is required. However, the degree of devi- ation from electro-neutrality is calculated to be smaller than ten orders of magnitude with respect to the equilibrium electrolyte concentration.
